newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai markets calm despite Moody's downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Thai markets calm despite Moody's downgrade.

text.p: Thai financial markets on Wednesday reacted coolly to news that Moody's Investors Service had downgraded Thailand's long term foreign currency debt ratings to A3 from A2.
Thai stocks dipped slightly in early dealings after the news broke but losses were small with some sales of banking counters. The stock index was down 3.07 points to 712.29 at 0419 GMT.

The baht was quoted weaker against the rising U.S. dollar at 26.107/117 at 0412 GMT from 26.090/095 late on Tuesday. But dealers attributed the slide mainly to the greenback's relentless march against other majors abroad.
The central bank earlier fixed the baht mid-rate against the dollar at 26.08, the lowest level since September 1989.
"This Moody's news was expected and there might be some knee-jerk reaction ... but its not going to be dramatic from the looks of things so far," said an analyst with a foreign brokerage.

Other analysts said one of the main side effects of the Moody's downgrade would be rising funding costs for Thai borrowers abroad. But the market had already discounted the downgrades and little market panic was expected.

Moody's also said that it had lowered the debt and deposit ratings of five Thai banks to A3 from A2. The banks downgraded were Bangkok Bank Plc, Industrial Finance Corporation of Thailand, Thai Farmers Bank Plc, Siam Commercial Bank Plc and the Export-Import Bank of Thailand.
The ratings agency said the cuts reflected concerns over the asset quality of banks in Thailand and the instability of the country's entire financial system.

Thai authorities last month ordered a revamp of the ailing domestic finance sector and told 10 weakened finance companies to boost their capital. They also asked all financial institutions to raise provisioning for sub-standard assets, mainly doubtful loans to the depressed Thai property sector.
